title: A Blue Window in the Snow

segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Sit tall without becoming rigid. Let the face soften and place gentle attention between the eyebrows.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [soft distant winter wind] Imagine a small blue window glowing in a house surrounded by snow. It is simply a visual anchor, not a supernatural claim.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice the dark space behind the eyelids around that window. Let the image remain small and easy.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Breathe naturally. With each exhale, imagine snow settling without needing the world to become silent.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Thoughts may leave footprints across the field. See them, then return to the blue window.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If the forehead tightens, release the image and feel the whole face. Return only when the point feels comfortable.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Rest with the window for several breaths. No need to look through it or discover what is inside.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] Attention can be both precise and gentle, like one lit square held by miles of soft weather.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let wandering be another snowfall. Notice it accumulating, then gently clear a path back.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Release effort for a moment and rest in the whole inner landscape, window included.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Begin feeling the body below the face... throat... chest... belly... hands... legs.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the snow scene fade while sounds and temperature return to the foreground.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Open your eyes when ready. Carry the steadiness of one quiet window into the room.
